quiz.q: What does passing `&s` (instead of `s`) to a function do?
options: Copies the whole String so the function gets its own
Lends a reference to s without giving up ownership
Moves s into the function permanently
Deletes s after the function runs
quiz.explain: `&s` borrows: the function gets a reference and can use the value, but ownership stays with the caller, so s is still usable afterward.

quiz.q: You have a read-only borrow `&String` and try to call `.push('!')` on it. What happens?
options: It works and changes the string
It compiles but does nothing at runtime
A compile error: you can't mutate through a `&` borrow
It makes a copy and mutates that
quiz.explain: A plain `&` borrow is read-only. To change the value you need a mutable borrow, `&mut`, and the original variable must be declared `mut`.

quiz.q: At one moment, for a single value, which combination of borrows is allowed?
options: One `&mut` and two `&` at the same time
Either many `&` readers OR one `&mut` writer, never both
quiz.explain: The borrowing rule: you may have many read-only borrows, or exactly one mutable borrow, but never a mutable borrow alongside any other borrow.

quiz.q: What three things must line up to mutate a value through a function?
options: The variable is `mut`, you pass `&mut`, the parameter is `&mut`
The variable is `const`, you pass `&`, the parameter is `String`
You call .clone(), pass by value, and return it
Nothing special; any `&` reference can mutate
quiz.explain: Mutable borrowing needs all three: the original declared `mut`, the value passed as `&mut`, and the parameter typed `&mut`.

flashcards.back: Using a value through a reference (&) without taking ownership. The function accesses the value and the original owner keeps it.
`&` is a read-only borrow (look, don't change). `&mut` is a mutable borrow (allowed to change the value), and the original must be `mut`.
At any one time you can have many immutable (&) borrows OR exactly one mutable (&mut) borrow of a value — never both together.
Borrowing moves and copies nothing — it's free. Cloning duplicates the whole value every time. Reach for & before reaching for .clone().
